title: Affine attracting strata for an isolated-fixed-point projective action
statement: Let $F$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure]. Let $X$ be a nonempty smooth connected projective $F$-scheme [def-pc-scheme, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-pc-projective-morphism], endowed with a $\mathbf G_m$-action, where $\mathbf G_m(A)=A^\times$ [def-sc-gm-ga]. Suppose an equivariant closed immersion into $\mathbf P(E)$ for a finite-dimensional linear $\mathbf G_m$-representation is given. Assume the fixed subscheme $X^{\mathbf G_m}$ is a finite disjoint union of reduced $F$-points. For each such point $x$, there is a unique smooth locally closed reduced subscheme $X_x^+\subseteq X$ whose $K$-points, for every algebraically closed extension $K/F$, are the points $y$ such that the orbit map $t\mapsto ty$ extends to $\mathbf A^1_K$ with value $x_K$ at zero. For every commutative $F$-algebra $A$, an $A$-point of $X_x^+$ is equivalently a $\mathbf G_{m,A}$-equivariant map $\mathbf A^1_A\to X_A$ with value $x_A$ at zero, by evaluation at $1$; here $\mathbf G_m$ acts on $\mathbf A^1$ by multiplication. These subschemes constitute a finite disjoint stratification, compatible with algebraically closed field extension. The scheme $X_x^+$ is isomorphic to $\mathbf A_F^{d_x}$, where $d_x$ is the dimension of the sum of the strictly positive character-weight spaces in $T_xX$. Here the weight $a\in\mathbf Z$ denotes the character $t\mapsto t^a$, and tangent space means the dual of $\mathfrak m_x/\mathfrak m_x^2$. Exactly one stratum is open dense, and it is the stratum at a fixed point whose entire tangent space has strictly positive weights. If $X=\operatorname{Spec}F$, its sole stratum is $\mathbf A^0_F$.

source.place: Theorem 13.47 and Corollaries 13.48--13.49, printed pp.272--274; projective linear-action application in the paragraph after Lemma 13.51, p.275. Projectivity is retained to ensure every orbit has a limit.

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-gm-representation-weight-basis], choose homogeneous coordinates $z_i$ on $\mathbf P(E)$ such that $t[z_i]=[t^{a_i}z_i]$. The standard chart $D_+(z_i)$ is affine by [lemma-nagata-relative-affine-space-open-immersion] (relabel its distinguished coordinate), with ratios $u_j=z_j/z_i$ of weights $a_j-a_i$. These charts are invariant. Their intersections $U_i$ with $X$ are affine by [def-weil-closed-immersion], and smooth by [lem-pc-open-immersion-smooth-composition]. Fix a fixed point $x$, choose $i$ with $z_i(x)\ne0$, and put $w=a_i$, $c_j=u_j(x)$. Since the line $x$ is fixed, $c_j=0$ if $a_j\ne w$. In this chart define $C_x$ by $u_j=0$ for $a_j<w$ and $u_j=c_j$ for $a_j=w$. Thus $C_x$ is an affine space on the remaining coordinates, all of strictly positive weights. Set $Y_x=X\cap C_x$ as a closed subscheme of $U_i$.

source.place: Lemma 13.46, p.272, and the affine concentrator equations of Definition 13.21/Proposition 13.24, pp.260--262.

proof.text: For every commutative $F$-algebra $A$, within $U_i$ the orbit of $y$ extends with value $x_A$ exactly when $u_j(y)=0$ for $a_j<w$ and $u_j(y)=c_j$ for $a_j=w$: its ratios are $t^{a_j-w}u_j(y)$. These identities hold even for nilpotent coefficients, since $A[t]\hookrightarrow A[t,t^{-1}]$ is injective. Hence $Y_x$ is the affine concentrator $U_i(\{x\})$ and is smooth of finite type by [lem-sfb-smooth-affine-concentrator]. Its immersion in $X$ is locally closed. Conversely, any equivariant $\phi:\mathbf A^1_A\to X_A$ with $\phi(0)=x_A$ factors through $(U_i)_A$: after every geometric base change, the inverse image of the invariant closed complement of $U_i$ is closed and invariant in $\mathbf A^1$ and misses zero. If it contained a nonzero point it would contain its whole $\mathbf G_m$-orbit and its closure, including zero, a contradiction. It is therefore empty on every fibre and hence empty. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-factors-through-open-subscheme] to factor $\phi$ through $U_i$, where the preceding polynomial equations apply. Conversely those equations give the equivariant extension by the same ratio formula; its defining equations for $X$ vanish in $A[t]$ because they vanish after inverting $t$. Thus evaluation at $1$ identifies $Y_x(A)$ with exactly the functor in the statement. Uniqueness inside the chart is part of the concentrator assertion. This also proves independence of the chosen chart by the identical functor.

source.place: Proposition 13.24 and Remark 13.57, pp.262,277; Proposition 13.58 and its proof, pp.277--278. The invariant-chart factorization is written out over arbitrary test algebras.

proof.text: Write $B=\mathcal O(Y_x)$. It is a quotient of the polynomial algebra on the strictly positive-weight coordinates of $C_x$. The action makes its defining ideal homogeneous: comparing coefficients in $F[t,t^{-1}]$ in the coaction of an invariant ideal places each homogeneous component in the ideal. Consequently $B=\bigoplus_{a\geq0}B_a$, $B_0=F$ (evaluation at $x$ preserves constants), and $\mathfrak m_x=\bigoplus_{a>0}B_a$. Smoothness from Step 2 and [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-scheme-over-field-regular] give regularity at this maximal ideal. Apply [lem-sfb-positive-graded-regular-polynomial] to homogeneous lifts of a basis of $\mathfrak m_x/\mathfrak m_x^2$. It gives $Y_x\cong\operatorname{Spec}F[T_1,\ldots,T_d]=\mathbf A^d_F$ by [def-sbc-affine-space]. In particular $Y_x$ is reduced.

source.place: Theorem 13.44, pp.271--272, in the fixed-point case; Lemma 13.39, pp.268--269.

proof.text:
The tangent calculation is scheme-theoretic: substitute $u_j=c_j+\epsilon v_j$ over $F[\epsilon]/(\epsilon^2)$. The equations of $C_x$ set $v_j=0$ exactly in the nonpositive-weight directions. The closed immersion $X\hookrightarrow\mathbf P(E)$ identifies $T_xX$ with the subspace satisfying the linear terms of its defining equations. Therefore
$$T_xY_x=T_xX\cap T_xC_x=(T_xX)_{>0}.$$
Indeed an invariant subspace of a diagonal representation is the direct sum of its weight intersections, by [lem-sfb-gm-representation-weight-basis]. The differential acts on $v_j$ by $t^{a_j-w}$; this is the stated tangent convention, with positive, not negative, weights. The tangent space of the polynomial algebra from Step 3 has basis dual to the classes of $T_i$, so its dimension is $d$. Thus $d=d_x$.

source.place: Corollaries 13.48--13.49(a), p.273, and the coordinate convention of Example 13.37, p.268.

proof.text:
For an algebraically closed extension $K/F$ and $y=[v]\in X(K)$, decompose $v=\sum_a v_a$ by weights and take $w$ to be the smallest weight with $v_w\ne0$. The expression
$$t\longmapsto[\sum_{a\geq w}t^{a-w}v_a]$$
is regular on $\mathbf A^1_K$: at least one weight-$w$ coordinate is a nonzero constant, so it lies in a standard chart. It lies in $X_K$, since every equation of the closed subscheme $X$ vanishes for $t\ne0$ and $K[t]\hookrightarrow K[t,t^{-1}]$ is injective. Its value at zero is $[v_w]$, a fixed point, hence one of the finitely many $x_K$ by the assumed fixed-subscheme description. Step 2 places $y$ in $Y_x(K)$. The minimum-weight formula determines this $x$ uniquely. Every point of $X$ lifts to a point over an algebraic closure of its residue field, so these descriptions prove exhaustion and pairwise disjointness of the underlying loci. They form the claimed finite partition by locally closed subschemes. All equations and the functor in Step 2 persist after algebraically closed scalar extension, giving the stated compatibility.

source.place: Proposition 13.20, pp.259--260; Theorem 13.47(c) and the appended erratum at p.273 requiring properness. Here the given projective embedding yields the limit explicitly.

proof.text: If another locally closed reduced subscheme has the prescribed points over every algebraically closed extension, it has the same support as $Y_x$: test each scheme point in an algebraic closure of its residue field. A locally closed reduced subscheme is the reduced induced structure on its support, by [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme] applied on opens where the support is closed. These opens cover the common support, so uniqueness there identifies the subschemes over $X$. Thus $X_x^+:=Y_x$ has the claimed uniqueness as well as the arbitrary-algebra description already proved.

source.place: Theorem 13.47(a), p.272; uniqueness as in Proposition 13.23, p.261.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-scheme-over-field-regular] and [lem-sc-regular-connected-integral], the nonempty smooth connected $X$ is integral, hence its underlying space is irreducible. The closures of the finitely many strata cover $X$. An irreducible space cannot be a finite union of proper closed subsets, so some stratum is dense. A dense locally closed subset is open: if it is $V\cap Z$ with $V$ open and $Z$ closed, density forces $Z=X$. Two such strata cannot exist since two nonempty opens in an irreducible space intersect. The reduced locally closed structure on this open is the open subscheme structure, by [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme]; $X$ is reduced. At its fixed point $x$, its tangent space is therefore $T_xX$, and Step 4 gives $T_xX=(T_xX)_{>0}$. This is the claimed attracting point and unique open dense stratum. Finally, for $X=\operatorname{Spec}F$, the action is trivial, the only tangent space is zero, and the construction has coordinate algebra $F$ and sole cell $\mathbf A^0_F$ by [def-sbc-affine-space].

source.place: Corollary 13.49(c) and proof, pp.273--274; dimension-zero case by the affine-space definition.

proof.text: Conversely, let $x'$ be any fixed point whose tangent weights are all strictly positive; we show that $X_{x'}^+$ is the open dense stratum $S$ of Step 7, so the fixed point named in the statement is unique. In the chart $U_i=\operatorname{Spec}A$ of $x'$ from Step 1, $Y_{x'}$ is cut out by the finitely many chart equations $g_1,\ldots,g_r\in A$ of $C_{x'}$. Let $\mathfrak p$ be the prime of $x'$, put $R=\mathcal O_{X,x'}=A_{\mathfrak p}$ with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$, and let $I\subseteq\mathfrak m$ be the ideal generated by the $g_k$, so $\mathcal O_{Y_{x'},x'}=R/I$ with maximal ideal $\bar{\mathfrak m}$. Both $X$ and $Y_{x'}$ are smooth over $F$ (Step 2), so $R$ and $R/I$ are regular local rings by [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-scheme-over-field-regular]. By Step 4, $T_{x'}Y_{x'}=(T_{x'}X)_{>0}=T_{x'}X$. Dually the surjection $\mathfrak m/\mathfrak m^2\to\bar{\mathfrak m}/\bar{\mathfrak m}^2$ is an isomorphism, so every element of $I$ has zero image in $\mathfrak m/\mathfrak m^2$. By [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-quotient-independent-generators], $I$ is generated by a finite set whose images in $\mathfrak m/\mathfrak m^2$ are linearly independent; such a set contains no element of zero image, so it is empty and $I=0$. Hence each $g_k$ is killed by some $s_k\in A\setminus\mathfrak p$, and on the open $D(s_1\cdots s_r)\ni x'$ of $U_i$ all equations of $Y_{x'}$ vanish: this nonempty open subscheme of $X$ lies in $X_{x'}^+$. It meets the open dense $S$ because $X$ is irreducible (Step 7), and distinct strata are disjoint (Step 5). Therefore $X_{x'}^+=S$ and $x'$ is its fixed point.

source.place: Corollary 13.49(c), pp.273--274 (uniqueness of the attracting point); Corollary 13.49(a) tangent-space identification, p.273.

proof_origin.place: Lemma 13.46, Theorem 13.44 and Section 13g proof of Theorem 13.47, pp.271--278; Corollary 13.49 and the appended properness erratum. Invariant projective charts make the gluing/functor argument explicit.

Uniqueness of reduced induced subschemes, used to identify locally closed strata from all geometric points.
Connected regular schemes are integral, used solely for the unique dense member of the finite locally closed partition.
